thread:
Elena (PM): Heads-up from three customer sessions: asks centered on non-disruptive canary traffic shaping for private installs, a lightweight operator-shim for legacy clusters, and explicit firewall/runbook steps for customer-managed NAT. Need to triage scope.
Vik (Eng): Can you list the top acceptance criteria for each?
Elena (PM): Sure. Canary shaping: ability to route X% traffic to new pods, observe key metrics for 10m, auto-cutover or auto-roll back on degradation. Operator-shim: a 1-file shim that exposes pause/resume API and supports older CRDs. Firewall/runbook: step-by-step NAT rules to preserve egress IPs and a validation packet-capture artifact.
Ruth (Field Eng): From RetailPilot: they want traffic split at L4 (TCP source IP preserved) not just DNS. Also need a way to test with synthetic load in staging that mirrors production.
Connor (SRE): Canary safety: require preflight to assert quorum and replication lag < threshold before enabling canary. Rollback must complete within 12m and not require manual DB intervention. Also add an "egress-constraint" telemetry tag.
Mai (Customer Success): Two enterprise customers said operator-shim is a blocker for them because they can't upgrade CRDs across clusters now. If shim is quick, it unlocks upgrades. They'll accept a shim + runbook for v1.
Vik (Eng): Implementation notes: traffic shaping can be implemented in operator via weighted service endpoints or by programmatic iptables rules. Weighted service endpoints simpler for k8s ingress cases; iptables needed for L4. Shim: small binary that translates legacy CRD fields to new API at runtime. Firewall runbook: documented iptables/nft rules + packet-capture helper that runs for N seconds and produces pcap.
Elena (PM): Proposal: sprint split: priority A (canary shaping POC + runbook for RetailPilot staging), priority B (operator-shim PoC + compatibility test), stretch (packet-capture helper + firewall runbook polish).
Ruth (Field Eng): Validation gates for canary shaping: 1) stage traffic split configurable (10/90, 50/50), 2) automated smoke test detects 5xxs and triggers rollback, 3) staging run with RetailPilot succeeds. I can run tests.
Connor (SRE): For operator-shim gates: 1) shim accepts legacy CRD versions and translates at runtime, 2) shim logs transformation events, 3) shim can be disabled without cluster restart. Also add an operator health metric.
Vik (Eng): Estimates: canary POC 3 pts, safety hooks + tests 2 pts, shim PoC 2 pts, packet-capture helper & docs 2 pts. Two engineers should be enough if we parallelize.
Mai (Customer Success): I'll schedule RetailPilot staging window and confirm acceptance criteria. Also will prepare customer-facing note about supported topologies and known limitations.
ci-bot: CI queued: operator/canary-shim #8810 -> awaiting runners.
Elena (PM): Action items: Vik to spike canary POC and open PR (EOW), Ruth to run staging harness and collect pcap when done, Connor to draft preflight checks and rollback SLA, Mai to confirm customer windows and prepare comms. Reconvene Friday 14:00 to decide final allocation. :sparkles:
